title: Mixture of Meta-Policies for Cross-Environment Meta-Reinforcement Learning

problem.claim: Meta-RL seeks to enable rapid adaptation to new tasks using prior experience from related tasks.

gap.claim: Existing Meta-RL approaches typically assume consistent state and action spaces, limiting generalization across environments with diverse morphologies, dynamics, and reward structures.

contributions.claim: MoMP is a modular and scalable Meta-RL framework for knowledge transfer across structurally heterogeneous environments.
MoMP represents policies as sparse combinations of shared attention-based policy submodules.
MoMP learns task-conditioned activation patterns that specialize and reuse attention modules across multiple environments.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the shared module can be plugged into new agents to accelerate learning on novel tasks.
The authors report that sparse activation improves adaptation speed and long-term retention by enabling targeted reuse and mitigating interference.
Experiments across diverse MuJoCo agents are reported to show significant improvement over strong meta-RL baselines in cross-environment generalization and meta-policy reuse.

narrative_sequence.summary: Meta-RL uses prior experience to support rapid adaptation to new tasks.
Conventional approaches are limited by assumptions of shared state and action spaces across tasks.
MoMP addresses the gap with sparse combinations of shared attention-based policy modules trained for task-conditioned specialization and reuse.
The trained shared module can be integrated into new agents to accelerate learning on novel tasks.
The authors report benefits from sparse activation and favorable results against meta-RL baselines on diverse MuJoCo agents.

source_observation.claim: Sparse combinations of shared modules are used to transfer knowledge across structurally heterogeneous environments.

interpretation.claim: Modular selective reuse may help separate transferable knowledge from environment-specific behavior.

application.claim: For systems spanning heterogeneous environments, consider shared reusable modules with task-conditioned sparse activation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach transfers beyond the reported MuJoCo-agent experiments.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark tasks, baseline identities, quantitative results, or statistical methodology.
The abstract does not describe how structurally heterogeneous observations and action interfaces are represented.
The abstract does not report computational costs, ablations, or failure cases.
